+        vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # int -> bytes
+        # count up the number of times every consecutive pair appears, keyed by
+        # the two-character string; kept up to date incrementally after each merge
+        stats = Counter(map(str.__add__, ids, ids[1:]))
+        for i in range(num_merges):
+            # find the pair with the highest count; ties go to the pair that
+            # occurs first in ids
+            top = max(stats.values(), default=0)
+            if not top:
+                raise IndexError("list index out of range")
+            cands = list(compress(stats, map(top.__eq__, stats.values())))
+            cpair = cands[0] if len(cands) == 1 else min(cands, key=ids.find)
+            pair = (ord(cpair[0]), ord(cpair[1]))
+            # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+            idx = 256 + i
+            c = chr(idx)
+            # update the pair counts around each run of adjacent occurrences
+            old = []
+            new = []
+            j = ids.find(cpair)
+            while j != -1:
+                s = j
+                e = j + 2
+                j = ids.find(cpair, e)
+                while j == e:
+                    e += 2
+                    j = ids.find(cpair, e)
+                lo = s - 1 if s else 0
+                seg = ids[lo:e + 1]
+                old.extend(map(str.__add__, seg, seg[1:]))
+                seg = ids[lo:s] + c * ((e - s) // 2) + ids[e:e + 1]
+                new.extend(map(str.__add__, seg, seg[1:]))
+            stats.subtract(Counter(old))
+            stats.update(new)
+            # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
+            ids = ids.replace(cpair, c)
+            # save the merge
+            merges[pair] = idx
+            vocab[idx] = vocab[pair[0]] + vocab[pair[1]]
+            # prints
+            if verbose:
+                print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")

actions.reason: BasicTokenizer.train counted every adjacent pair of the whole sequence again on each merge. Now the counts are built once, keyed by the two-character string. After each merge only the pairs touched by it are updated. The code finds each run of adjacent non-overlapping occurrences with str.find, the same left-to-right scan str.replace uses. For each run it subtracts the pairs of the old segment (with one neighbour character on each side) and adds the pairs of the merged segment. The pair chosen is the same as before: the highest count, with ties going to the pair that occurs first in the current sequence. That is the order Counter.most_common gave on a freshly built Counter. Merges and vocab come out identical.

journal.text:
I changed BasicTokenizer.train in minbpe/basic.py, lines 35-51, plus one line at line 13. Before the change it recounted every adjacent pair of the whole sequence on each merge. Now the counts are built once, keyed by the two-character string. After each merge only the pairs touched by that merge are updated. Runs of non-overlapping occurrences are found with str.find, scanning left to right the same way str.replace does.

My sandbox evaluation was accepted, with identical outputs. train_basic_ir went from 2102615613 to 861430062, ratio 0.4097. The other metrics barely moved: train_regex_ir 1.0007, encode_ir 1.0006, decode_ir 1.0030, save_load_ir 1.0031. The guard passed on 1 file, 39 lines. This is my measurement only. Replays decide the verdict.

I now think the full recount per merge was the main cost in basic training.

Next, I want to try the same incremental counting in the regex tokenizer's train, which this change did not touch.
